 Batter ruled out of India’s third T20I against New Zealand
 The 28-year-old is set to miss the Wellington T20I as he continues his recovery from injury.
 26 October, 2026 Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of India’s third T20I of the five-match series against New Zealand, set to be played on October 27.
 Kishan sustained the injury during the first T20I of the series and is recovering well, as confirmed by the BCCI. 
 However, the wicketkeeper-batter is yet to regain match fitness, with the BCCI Medical Team continuing to monitor his progress.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra, who is part of the India A squad currently touring New Zealand, joined the T20I squad as cover ahead of the second T20I and will remain with the team for the third game as Kishan continues his rehabilitation.
 Teenage prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had taken over the No. 3 spot in the second clash, where  India sealed the deal in a thriller .
 Update 
Ishan Kishan is recovering well from his low grade right adductor strain, which he sustained during the first T20I of the series against New Zealand. 
He is yet to regain match fitness and is ruled out of the third T20I to be played on October 27, 2026 in Wellington.…
— BCCI (@BCCI) October 26, 2026 
 Series schedule: 
 First T20I: 22 October, Christchurch (India won by four wickets) 
 Second T20I: 24 October, Christchurch (India won by four wickets) 
 Third T20I: 27 October, Wellington
 Fourth T20I: 30 October, Auckland
 Fifth T20I: 1 November, Hamilton
